question.worked_solution:
We use the quotient rule with the numerator $u(x)={x}^{3}$ and the denominator $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1).$ 

Differentiating $u(x)$ and $v(x),$ we have

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=3{x}^{2},\,{v}^{′}(x)=\frac{2}{2x+1}.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the quotient rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(3{x}^{2})(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1))-({x}^{3})(\frac{2}{2x+1})}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{2x+1}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1))}^{2}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
